scientific_facts.source: Multiple aquarium nutrition studies + globalseafood.org + fishtankhobbyist.com
key_facts: Opened fish food loses fat-soluble vitamins (A, E) and water-soluble vitamins (C, B1) through oxidation within 1-3 months
Highly unsaturated fatty acids form unstable free radicals and peroxides when exposed to air
Flake food loses nutritional potency fastest — within 30 days of opening
Signs of expired food: faded color, rancid smell, clumping from moisture, fish refusal to eat
Fish fed oxidized food show decreased growth and increased oxidative stress
Store in airtight container, cool dark place, and buy small quantities that can be consumed within 6 months

title: كيف تعرف سمكتك مريضة
anti_ai_global: All prompts use: natural film grain, slight lens dust, realistic shadows, imperfect edges, phone camera EXIF metadata. Avoid: oversmoothed, plastic-like, digitally rendered, cartoonish, perfect symmetry, AI sheen.

scientific_facts.source: Multiple veterinary aquarium health databases + petbarn.com.au + chewy.com + buceplant.com
key_facts: Sign 1 — Clamped fins: fish holds fins tight against body = universal stress/disease indicator
Sign 2 — White spots (Ich/Ichthyophthirius multifiliis): small salt-grain white dots = parasitic infection, highly contagious
Sign 3 — Gasping at surface: fish hovering at waterline gulping air = low oxygen, ammonia burn, or gill infection
Other signs: loss of appetite, erratic swimming, faded colors, hiding, bloating, fin rot
Root cause #1 is always poor water quality — test ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, pH first
Immediate action: 25% water change + test water parameters + quarantine sick fish

title: درجة الحرارة المثالية لكل سمكة
anti_ai_global: All prompts use: natural film grain, slight lens dust, realistic shadows, imperfect edges, phone camera EXIF metadata. Avoid: oversmoothed, plastic-like, digitally rendered, cartoonish, perfect symmetry, AI sheen.
brand_note: AQUAVO = educational and approachable, not dramatic or fear-based. Show common mistakes gently → then show the solution with pride. Never show graphic fish suffering.

scientific_facts.source: Multiple aquarium care databases + aquariumstoredepot.com + petmd.com + buceplant.com + advancedaquariumconcepts.com
key_facts: Goldfish: 18-22°C (65-72°F) — COLDWATER species, NOT tropical. Higher temps increase metabolism unnaturally, halve lifespan, increase waste production
Guppy/Platy/Molly: 22-26°C (72-79°F) — tropical, adaptable, best at 24-25°C
Betta: 25-27°C (78-81°F) — tropical, needs heater always, gets lethargic in cold water
Neon Tetra: 22-26°C (72-78°F) — prefers cooler tropical, sensitive to temperature swings
Corydoras: 22-25.5°C (72-78°F) — cooler end of tropical range
Goldfish produce 3-5x more waste than tropical fish of same size — need strong filtration and cooler water
Betta + Goldfish in same tank = INCOMPATIBLE on every level (temp, aggression, waste, pH preference)
Temperature stability more important than exact degree — fluctuations cause immune suppression and stress
General tropical community: 24-26°C (75-78°F)
Common Iraqi home mistake: goldfish + guppies in one small tank at room temp (30°C+ in summer) — goldfish suffers, all fish stressed

scientific_facts.source: Multiple planted tank resources + aquariumcoop.com + buceplant.com + virtual-aquarium.com
key_facts: Anubias nana: attach to rocks/wood, NEVER bury rhizome, extremely hardy, low light, no CO2
Java Fern (Microsorum pteropus): attach to hardscape, propagates from leaf tips, very forgiving
Java Moss (Taxiphyllum barbieri): tie to wood/rock, grows in any light, provides fry cover
Cryptocoryne wendtii: root feeder (use root tabs), may melt initially then recovers strong
Vallisneria: grass-like background plant, spreads by runners, hardy in low light, grows tall fast
All 5 plants: no CO2 injection needed, no expensive fertilizers, thrive on fish waste nutrients
Key rule: epiphytes (Anubias, Java Fern, Java Moss) = attach to hardscape; rooted (Crypto, Vals) = plant in substrate
